newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore's Popular plans bookstore expansion.
newsitem.headline: Singapore's Popular plans bookstore expansion.

text.p: Singapore's leading bilingual bookstore operator Popular Holdings Ltd is planning a chain of up to 200 bookstores in Asia, company chairman Chou Cheng Ngok said on Wednesday.

Popular, which on Wednesday launched its initial public share offer (IPO) of 75 million new shares at Singapore $0.36 (US$0.25) each, has 77 outlets in Singapore, Malaysia and Hong Kong. About half are franchise outlets.
Chou, speaking at the IPO launch, gave no time frame for Popular to reach the 200 store target but said the group's plan was to open at least eight new outlets a year.
Book retailing contributes about 40 percent of group net profits, which reached S$5.76 million on turnover of S$126.36 million for the financial year ended April 30, 1996.
For the financial year ending April 30, 1997, the group has forecast an 18 percent rise in net profit to S$6.8 million and turnover of S$165.9 million.
Besides selling books, Popular has a thriving book publishing arm in Hong Kong which publishes general interest books and has a library of more than 5,000 titles.
Chou said publishing contributed about 60 percent of group profits and Popular planned to start publishing educational text books in Singapore and Malaysia by next year.
Chou, who is based in Hong Kong, said he hoped to retain the current ratio of retail's contribution to profits at 40 percent and publishing at 60 percent.

With net proceeds of about S$25.3 million raised from the IPO, the company plans to build a new warehouse and office in Singapore, repay some bank borrowings, invest in a publishing unit, open new stores and use the balance as working capital.
Chou said Popular was also aiming to expand into the office stationery market in Singapore, estimated to be worth about S$400 million a year.
"The market is very fragmented at the moment...We hope to get 10-20 percent of the market in the next two years," he said.
While the group's operations in Singapore and Hong Kong were profitable last year, Malaysia's operations were in the red with a S$600,000 loss because of high start-up costs.
Popular director Khang Swee Cheng said the group should break even in Malaysia for the financial year ending April 30, 1997, and is expected to turn a profit in the next financial year.
